title: Shear and Bending-Moment Analysis of a Hydraulically Supported Industrial Robot Arm
summary: A robot-arm beam problem integrating two-force-member modeling, whole-arm equilibrium, hydraulic-cylinder force, pin reactions, piecewise shear and moment functions, diagrams, and critical-section identification.
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference idealization of a horizontal robot arm with a left free overhang, pin A, hydraulic cylinder at B, end load at C, uniform load, and symbolic geometry.
problemStatement:
A hydraulically actuated industrial manipulator holds a payload while stationary. Its horizontal arm carries a uniform downward load representing arm and gripper weight, plus a concentrated payload at C.

For the beam model, coordinate s is measured from the left free tip. Pin A is at s = a, cylinder attachment B is at s = a + b, and C is at s = a + b + L. Cylinder BD is an ideal two-force member.
engineeringGoal: Determine the hydraulic-cylinder force and pin reactions, derive and construct the arm's shear-force and bending-moment diagrams, and identify the location and magnitude of the absolute maximum bending moment.
